basics.summary: I work at the interface of cosmology and galaxy evolution, using cosmological hydrodynamical simulations to study the connection between active galactic nuclei (AGN), their host galaxies and their dark matter halos. I model this co-evolution with halo occupation distributions and conditional luminosity functions, and I am interested in statistics beyond the two-point function, such as k-nearest-neighbour distributions.

work.name: Presidency University, Kolkata
work.summary: Advisor: Dr. Suchetana Chatterjee. Tentative thesis: Large Scale Structures in the High Redshift Universe. PhD expected January 2027.
highlights: Quasar halo occupation in simulations: measured the halo occupation distribution of quasars in IllustrisTNG and SIMBA and its dependence on luminosity, redshift, black hole mass and feedback mode. Showed that the central occupation of luminous AGN is suppressed in massive halos, and that a standard HOD fit to clustering can bias the inferred host halo mass.

AGN conditional luminosity functions: modelled the AGN conditional luminosity function in TNG300 for 0.1 < z < 3, and developed a joint MCMC framework that fits the luminosity function and two-point correlation function together to recover the host halos of quasars.

Beyond two-point statistics (ongoing, with Prof. Arka Banerjee): testing whether k-nearest-neighbour cumulative distribution functions recover the galaxy– and AGN–halo connection in TNG300 where projected two-point fits fail.
